subject: Clarify DPA: Swiss export risks & backup-access controls
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novasec.ch>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal+privacy@novasec.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 17:12:00 +0200
Subject: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the DPA draft — quick set of questions from our privacy team at NovaSec AG. We are a Switzerland-based processor for our customers, and our internal counsel is asking for clarity on two items before we proceed:

1) Backups & export exposure: your draft references replication to multi-region blob stores. Can you confirm whether backups of Swiss-origin data could be accessible from the US in an incident/recovery scenario? The language in the DPA is high-level and we'd like concrete technical controls or contractual limits (TIA/DTIA language) to rely on.

2) Subprocessor access: we require a short window to review any new subprocessor before activation (5 business days). Is that feasible? If not, please propose an alternate SLA.

3) UK/EEA mapping: we operate clients with EEA and UK residency; please confirm whether you will rely on SCCs, UK IDTA/UK addendum, or both for different customers — and whether you can sign an additional TIA scoped to NovaSec's processing.

Attached: our standard Data Residency questionnaire (we filled what we could).

Can we hop on a short call if helpful — otherwise a written response is fine.

Best,
Anna Müller
Head of Privacy, NovaSec AG
anna.mueller@novasec.ch
+41 44 555 0132

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novasec.ch>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then more detail below:

1) Backups: our production backups are replicated to an encrypted multi-region store. For EU/CH-origin data we maintain region-aware replication; that said, in the event of a global disaster-recovery activation, there is a documented DR runbook that could require recovery operations in a US-managed region. We are happy to: (a) add a contractual commitment that Redwood will not intentionally restore Swiss-origin customer data in the US except for emergency DR declared by our SOC/CTO (and then only under supervisory review), and (b) provide a TIA addendum describing technical mitigations (encryption-in-transit, HSM key residency options, and access gating).

2) Subprocessor review window: 5 business days is reasonable for standard categories. We typically use a 10-day notice SLA in our standard DPA but can commit to 5 days for NovaSec (documented in an addendum).

3) Transfer mechanisms: we use a combination — standard EU SCCs for EEA data, and the UK IDTA + Redwood addendum for UK-resident data. For Switzerland-sourced data we propose: SCCs + a bespoke TIA describing our retention/backup carveouts. We will not require separate signature on the SCCs if your counsel prefers a single DPA with annexed transfer addenda.

I'll loop in Kimberly (legal) and Naomi (infrastructure) who can answer the technical specifics and provide the marked DPA and subprocessor matrix. If you prefer a call, I'm available Wed afternoon next week.

–Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
rm@redwoodinference.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novasec.ch>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Anna — thanks, this is the right thread. I'm attaching a redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_marked.pdf) and our current Q3 subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_Q3_2025.csv). Key notes:

- Backups: operationally we shard backups by region; however, our disaster recovery (DR) process can trigger cross-region restoration. We will add contractual language: "Redwood will not execute cross-border restoration of customer-specific backups except where (i) a DR event is declared by Redwood's Incident Commander, and (ii) Redwood has documented reasonable efforts to restore within-region before cross-region recovery." We can also include an obligation to notify NovaSec within 48 hours of any cross-region restore and to provide logs of which engineer/service performed the action.

- Access controls: all backup decryption keys for EEA/CH customer buckets will be managed under a KMS policy; keys may be HSM-backed and we offer an option for customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private plans.

- Subprocessors: we can accept a 5 business day review window for new subprocessors for NovaSec customers. For vendors that are time-sensitive (security patches, CDN changes) we will offer a temporary "expedited activation" path but with post-activation review and rollback rights.

Please review the redline; Naomi, could you confirm the DR runbook excerpt (where cross-region restores are used) and whether we can attach an anonymized log sample for auditing?

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Kimberly / Rishi — pulled the relevant DR excerpt and answering the technical asks:

- DR operations: the DR playbook triggers cross-region restores only when a whole-region service outage is declared (e.g., region-level storage corruption). In such cases, recovery may be performed from a geographically separate replica.

- Access logs: we can provide a redacted sample of our restore audit trail (who/when/source namespace). It includes S3-style object replication logs, KMS key usage logs, and the incident ticket id. We will not share full production logs but can offer a 90-day redacted window for audit.

- Mitigation options: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) prevents Redwood from being able to decrypt backups without explicit customer action. This is available on Redwood Dedicated and Private; for Hosted customers we can offer HSM-backed KMS with strict access controls and dual-approval for export/restore flows.

I'll prepare a short TIA addendum draft that enumerates the above controls and the notification SLA. Kimberly — will include the TIA as an annex to the DPA redline.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novasec.ch>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal+privacy@novasec.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:17:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Kimberly / Naomi — thanks for the thorough responses and the redline. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

- The DR carveout language looks acceptable, but we want an additional sentence: "Redwood will, where reasonably practicable, prefer in-country or in-region recovery and will document why cross-region recovery was necessary." Can you add that?

- For the 5-business day subprocessor review, we need the ability to veto any new subprocessor for our NovaSec-managed customers for security-sensitive categories within that window (e.g., logging, key management). We expect limited use but need the contractual right.

- The TIA annex: would you include a short table that maps the control (KMS residency, HSM option, dual-approval restore) to the technical evidence you can provide (e.g., audit log samples, architecture diagram, SOC2 control IDs)?

We can sign once the above additions are reflected. If it's easier, feel free to cut a one-page addendum and we'll circulate internally.

Regards,
Anna

Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: Swiss data flows and backups

Anna — thanks, that's helpful and reasonable. We'll: (1) add the suggested sentence about preferring in-region recovery and requiring a written rationale when cross-region restore occurs; (2) accept (with limited carveouts) a NovaSec veto right for security-sensitive categories during the 5-day review window — we'll propose a process where vetoes must be raised with a written rationale and metadata (scope, tech concern), and Redwood will either accept or propose a mitigation within 5 business days; (3) include the TIA mapping table linking controls to evidence (SOC2 section references, sample audit extract, and architecture diagram).

We'll produce a single-page DPA addendum that bundles the DR carveout, subprocessor review/veto process, and the TIA mapping table. Rishi will send the addendum as a DocuSign once legal signs off.

Next steps: Kimberly to circulate the one-page addendum for internal legal approval (ETA 48 hours). Rishi to schedule a short sync next Wed if NovaSec would like to review live.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
